# lambda-trigger-apigw

Creates an HTTP API (API Gateway v2) that routes requests to a Lambda function. Supports optional custom domain and JWT authorizer.

## Usage

```hcl
module "api_gateway" {
  source = "../../modules/lambda-trigger-apigw"

  function_name = module.my_function.function_name
  function_arn  = module.my_function.function_arn
  invoke_arn    = module.my_function.invoke_arn

  routes = [
    "GET /users",
    "POST /users",
    "GET /users/{id}",
  ]
}
```

## IAM Model

This is a **push-based** trigger. The module creates an `aws_lambda_permission` resource-based policy allowing API Gateway to invoke the function. No IAM role attachment is needed.

## Inputs

### Required

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `function_name` | `string` | Name of the Lambda function. Used for resource naming and the Lambda permission. |
| `function_arn` | `string` | ARN of the Lambda function. |
| `invoke_arn` | `string` | Invocation ARN of the Lambda function. Obtained from the core module's `invoke_arn` output. Used by the API Gateway integration. |
| `routes` | `list(string)` | List of route keys. Each entry follows the format `METHOD /path`. Greedy path parameters are supported. Examples: `"GET /users"`, `"POST /users"`, `"GET /users/{id}"`, `"ANY /v1/{proxy+}"`, `"$default"`. |

### Optional

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `stage_name` | `string` | `"$default"` | Name of the API Gateway stage. The `$default` stage auto-deploys and serves traffic at the root URL. Named stages serve traffic under `/<stage_name>/`. |
| `custom_domain` | `object` | `null` | Custom domain configuration. When `null` (default), no domain resources are created. When provided, all fields are required. |
| `authorizer` | `object` | `null` | JWT authorizer configuration. When `null` (default), routes are unauthenticated. When provided, all routes use the JWT authorizer. Only the JWT type is supported — REQUEST authorizers (custom Lambda authorizers) are not supported. |
| `tags` | `map(string)` | `{}` | Map of tags applied to all resources (API, stage, domain, authorizer). |

**`custom_domain` object fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `domain_name` | `string` | The custom domain name (e.g. `api.example.com`). A Route53 A-record alias is created pointing to the API Gateway domain. |
| `hosted_zone_id` | `string` | Route53 hosted zone ID for the domain. |
| `certificate_arn` | `string` | ARN of an ACM certificate covering the domain name. The certificate must already exist (BYO). |

**`authorizer` object fields:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Name of the authorizer (e.g. `"cognito"`, `"auth0"`). Displayed in the AWS console. |
| `issuer` | `string` | Yes | The issuer URL of the OIDC provider. For Cognito: `https://cognito-idp.<region>.amazonaws.com/<user-pool-id>`. For Auth0: `https://<tenant>.auth0.com/`. Must be a valid HTTPS URL. |
| `audience` | `list(string)` | Yes | List of allowed audience values (client IDs). Tokens must contain at least one of these values in the `aud` claim. For Cognito, use the User Pool Client ID. |
| `identity_sources` | `list(string)` | No | Token location(s) for the authorizer. Default: `["$request.header.Authorization"]`. Other examples: `["$request.querystring.token"]`. |

## Outputs

| Name | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `api_id` | ID of the HTTP API. |
| `api_endpoint` | Default API Gateway endpoint URL (e.g. `https://<id>.execute-api.<region>.amazonaws.com`). |
| `execution_arn` | Execution ARN of the HTTP API. Useful for constructing permission source ARNs. |
| `stage_id` | ID of the API Gateway stage. |
| `custom_domain_url` | Custom domain URL (e.g. `https://api.example.com`). `null` if no custom domain is configured. |
| `authorizer_id` | ID of the JWT authorizer. `null` if no authorizer is configured. |
